esbuild.Build({entry: app.tsx, bundle:true, format:'esm', target:'es2020', external:['bm','sdui']}) - es2020 means no top-level await in a module
The built bundle is cached per entry path until any bundled input's mtime changes (inputs are checked at most once a second).

Caching: browsers get `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, must-revalidate` with an ETag, so a reload revalidates (304) instead of re-downloading, and CDNs get no-store; the bundle is served pre-gzipped. `/static/app.js?v=<tree>` as the framework writes it into pages is public and immutable for a year only when `v` matches the build; any other `v` gets the revalidated response.

Other static files: a static/ file is public and immutable for a year only when its query is exactly the `?v=` the framework writes for its current bytes (for a .js file, the static/ tree version), as served HTML carries. Every other request - no query (an `` in a .tsx view, a CSS url(), a direct link), a stale or hand-written `?v=2`, any other query - is `public, no-cache` with a content ETag and revalidates (304 while the bytes are unchanged, even after a promote rewrites the file). The PWA manifest's /static/ icon carries the version too. Cloudflare in front of hosted apps can store a bare /static/ URL for a while whatever the origin sends, so check a direct link with `curl -sI` (cf-cache-status, age) before assuming a push did not land.

On a build error the URL answers 200 with a module that only throws the esbuild message (the console shows it; the page's HTML loads but none of that bundle's code runs). Push and `benmore check` build the same bundles first and refuse what would fail; see compile_errors.

While a reviewed mcp.yaml is loaded (the create_app starter and the self-hosted `benmore new` starter have one; a reload whose source no longer matches the review turns the connector off and serves the directory again, see api(at:"connector")), static/ files, compiled bundles and pages are served from the source the app last loaded, not from the directory: a file changed on disk is served after the next reload (a push or deploy reloads the app), and a file added since the last load answers 404 until then. The `?v=` rule is the same, with versions taken from that loaded source: a file's `?v=` is the hash of the bytes being served, a .js file's `?v=` covers the app's whole reviewed source (it changes when any source file changes or the runtime is upgraded), and exactly that URL is public and immutable for a year. Every other request - no query, a stale or hand-written `?v=`, any other query - is `private, no-cache, must-revalidate` with a content ETag and CDN no-store, at /static/<path> and at the root-relative /<path> alike.

esbuild strips TypeScript types without checking them, so a type error (`const n: number = 'x'`, `bm.table('typo')`) compiles, pushes and passes `benmore check`, then fails at runtime (a 404 from /api/typo). Type errors show in your editor, or run `tsc --noEmit` in the app directory: tsconfig.json maps `bm` to src/bm.d.ts.

The write gate refuses the files of a Node toolchain, because there is no npm step: package.json and lockfiles (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb), .npmrc/.yarnrc/.pnpmrc, anything under node_modules/, a webpack, vite, rollup or esbuild config file and hand-written dist/ or build/ output. To use a library, copy its ES module files under static/ and import them relatively. It also refuses a tsconfig.json with `"noEmit": false` or `"baseUrl"`, a desktop metadata sidecar (`._*`, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db) and types/bm.d.ts, which the framework generates.
